the set of spherical harmonic coefficient weightings that are used for the generalized moment concentration criterion are not the same as the set of frequency weightings used for the fourth-moments.

for a given frequency weighting, the optimal signal energy concentration problem for the sphere is solved using the generalized moment criterion, and that for a given time-frequency weighting, the optimal time-frequency energy concentration problem for time-frequency analysis on the time axis is solved using the fourth moment bandwidth measure.

, for the fourth-momentum bandwidth measure, the classical Slepians are the best functions for the spatially limited signals on the 1-sphere (circle) while the minimum bandwidth functions are best for the 2-spheres.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

for the 2-spheric signal energy concentration problem, the classical Slepians are the best functions to use, but for the time-frequency concentration problem, the minimum bandwidth functions are better.
for the classical Slepians, the fourth-moment criterion is the optimal choice, but for the generalized Slepians, this criterion is not optimal.
the generalized moment concentration measure is more sensitive to the spatially-limited signals on the sphere than the classical moment measure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the generalized spectral concentration problem can be used to design signals that are spatially localized and that have a specified frequency content.
the generalized moment criterion is not a good measure for spectral concentration of signals in the spherical domain.
the classical Slepain functions are not optimal under the generalized moment criterion on the 2sphere.
